title: Performance-Portable Symbolic Factorization through Common Graph Operations
problem: Symbolic factorization in sparse LU decomposition is essential for understanding sparsity patterns and fill-ins, but existing approaches rely on specialized graph algorithms that are difficult to port efficiently across diverse hardware.
motivation: GraphBLAS provides a standard interface for graph operations in linear algebra, enabling portable performance. Using GraphBLAS for symbolic factorization could enable efficient execution across multi-core and many-core architectures without architecture-specific rewrites.
method: Express edge-based and path-based symbolic factorization using common GraphBLAS operations. Investigate use of masks and elimination trees for optimization. Evaluate on multi-core and many-core architectures for various sparse matrices.
key_novelty: Novel application of GraphBLAS standard for symbolic factorization; demonstration of portable performance across heterogeneous architectures using high-level linear algebra abstractions.
contributions: Expression of symbolic factorization using standard GraphBLAS operations
Efficient mask and elimination tree utilization for optimization
Portable implementation executing efficiently on both multi-core and many-core systems
Evaluation on diverse sparse matrices and architectures
limitations: Limited performance comparison with highly optimized sparse libraries (e.g., SuperLU, PARDISO); scalability to very large matrices not detailed; overhead of GraphBLAS abstraction not quantified.
